exampleAnswers.title: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations

question.text:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \,$ and $\, R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1?$

\[ A = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right], \qquad B = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 0 & 1 \\ 2& 0 \end{array}\right], \qquad C = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right] \]
question.explanation:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

\begin{align*} A & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & \leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array}\right] \\[5pt] &\neq I \quad {\color{red} \times} \\[10pt] B & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 0 & 1 \\ 2& 0 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & \leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] \\[5pt] &= I \quad {\color{green}\checkmark} \\[10pt] C & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & \leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{array}\right] \\[5pt] &\neq I \quad {\color{red} \times} \end{align*}

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

\[ A = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 4 \end{array}\right], \qquad B = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 7 & 2 \\ 3& 1 \end{array}\right], \qquad C = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 9 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array}\right] \]

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations

question.text:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $A^{-1}.$

\begin{align*} [A\,|\,I \,] & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+(-3) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1& 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3& 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2& := \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \\ 0 & 1 & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \end{array}\right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [A\,|\,I \,] & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+(-3) R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1& 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3& 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:=(-1) R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1& 0\\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -1 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, \[ A^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.explanation:
We write down $Q$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Q$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [Q\,|\,I \,] & = \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 & := R_2+(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & \, 4 & \; 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \! -1 & \!-1 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= \left(-1\right)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 4 & 1& 0\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right] & R_1 & := R_1 + (-4)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & -3& 4\\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $P$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $P^{-1}.$

\begin{align*} [P\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} -3 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_1 & := -\dfrac{1}{3}R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= R_2+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3} &- \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{2}{3}& 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{3}{5}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3}& -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5} \end{array} \right] & R_1& := \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \\ 0 & 1 & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \end{array}\right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $P$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $P$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [P\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} -3 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_1 & := -\dfrac{1}{3}R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= R_2+(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3} &- \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{2}{3}& 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= \dfrac{3}{5}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{1}{3}& -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5} \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:=R_1+ \dfrac{1}{3}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0& -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5} \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The matrix $P^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, \[ P^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{3}{5} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

\begin{align*} [Y\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3& 4 \\ \end{array} \right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [Y\,|\,I \,] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 4 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= R_1 +R_2\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2+3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3& 4 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}

The corresponding row operations are \[ R_1 := R_1 +R_2, \quad R_2 := R_2+3R_1. \]

The matrix $Y^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

\[ Y^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1\\ 3& 4 \\ \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
The inverse of the matrix $U$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

\begin{align*} [U\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0& 3& -1 \\ 0 & 1 &-2 & 1 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $U$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $U$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [U\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= R_2+(-2)R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:= R_1+(-1)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0& 3& -1 \\ 0 & 1 &-2 & 1 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The corresponding row operations are \[ R_2 := R_2+(-2)R_1, \qquad R_1 := R_1+(-1)R_2. \]

The matrix $U^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

\[ U^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} 3& -1 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
The inverse of the matrix $K$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

\begin{align*} [K\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} -3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:= -\dfrac{1}{3}R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} &-\frac{2}{3} & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= 3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & - \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & - 3 & 4\\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $K$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $K$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [K\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} -3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:= -\dfrac{1}{3}R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= R_2+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} &-\frac{2}{3} & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= 3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -\frac{4}{3} & - \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:=R_1+\dfrac{4}{3}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & - 3 & 4\\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The corresponding row operations are \[ R_1 := -\dfrac{1}{3}R_1, \qquad {\color{blue}R_2 := R_2+2R_1}, \qquad R_2 := 3R_2, \qquad {\color{blue}R_1 :=R_1+\dfrac{4}{3}R_2}. \]

The matrix $K^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

\[ K^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} - 3 & 4\\ -2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
The inverse of the matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

\begin{align*} [B\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{array} \right] & & \text{___________} \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{array} \right] \end{align*}
question.explanation:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

\begin{align*} [B\,|\,I] & = \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:= -\dfrac{1}{3}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{array} \right] & R_1 &:= R_1+2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[ \begin{array}{cc|cc} 1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{array} \right] \end{align*}

The corresponding row operations are \[ R_2:= \dfrac{1}{3}R_2, \qquad R_1:= R_1+2R_2. \]

The matrix $B^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

\[ B^{-1}= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix}. \]
